--- PART 1/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Use these measurements when deciding what to retain or change to maximize cumulative tournament fitness."
STRATEGY: The parent is a TFT-like strategy: first 3 C, then D if last opp D, C if opp_defects==0, D if opp_defects>=3 and opp_defects*3>=n, C if my_defects > opp_defects+2, C if last_my D and last_opp C, else C. The trace simulates the parent against controlled probes (one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D) and considers changes to improve forgiveness, retaliation, and exploitation.

--- PART 2/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Exactly the measured score! So my simulation is correct."
STRATEGY: The parent is a hand-coded strategy with rules: cooperate initially, defect if last opponent move was D, defect if opponent has defected at least 3 times and opp_defects*3 >= n, cooperate if own defections exceed opponent's by more than 2, cooperate if last own move was D and last opponent move was C, otherwise cooperate. The trace simulates this parent against periodic_D, one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, and sustained_D, then designs a revised strategy (forgive first defection, retaliate on streaks, exploit opponent cooperation while defecting, break long DD cycles, and always defect after long opponent defection streaks) to improve cumulative tournament fitness.

--- PART 3/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "This is much better than parent's 2.375, and close to optimal 3.33." and "The parent got 0.9583 by never breaking. So we lose 0.0417 against sustained_D."
STRATEGY: The parent is a forgiving TFT with exploitation and probing; the trace simulates it against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, and periodic_D, then revises it by adding a last-round defection, a one-time probe against never-defecting opponents, and a break-out condition when both sides have defected at least three times.
